question: I'm building a little space shooter in the browser, just me on weekends, and I'm using Phaser. Where do I start?
lines: {"say": "Start with one playable scene: move your ship, shoot bullets, and destroy an enemy."}
{"say": "Start with one Phaser scene: a ship that moves and a single enemy to shoot."}
{"say": "Wire arrow keys to movement and spacebar to bullets, using plain shapes instead of finished artwork."}
{"say": "Use Phaser\u2019s Arcade Physics for collisions, so bullets destroy enemies and touching an enemy ends the run."}
{"say": "Then add a score and a restart button; that gives you a complete little game before adding more enemies."}
{"say": "Skip accounts, multiplayer, and fancy art for now; aim for thirty seconds that feels fun."}
{"say": "Have you already got Phaser running in your browser, or are you starting from an empty folder?"}

question: Okay, I've got a ship flying around and enemies coming at me. Now I want accounts and a global leaderboard. Firebase or Supabase?
lines: {"say": "That comes down to Firebase\u2019s document model versus Supabase\u2019s SQL flexibility for leaderboard queries."}
{"say": "Firebase gives you easy accounts and realtime updates, but leaderboard queries need more planning with Firestore."}
{"say": "Supabase also handles accounts, and its SQL database makes rankings straightforward, though you\u2019ll need access policies."}
{"say": "For your weekend shooter, I lean Supabase because querying scores and rankings fits SQL naturally."}
{"say": "Either way, accounts don\u2019t prevent cheating; your backend should validate submitted scores rather than trusting the browser."}
{"say": "Does Supabase sound good, or are you already more comfortable with Firebase?"}

question: I've used Firebase before, so let's go Firebase. How do scores get into the leaderboard without people cheating?
lines: {"say": "Never trust the client; validate the score on the server using Firebase Functions."}
{"say": "With Firebase, send results to a Cloud Function that checks submissions before writing to your leaderboard in Firestore."}
{"say": "Require Firebase Authentication, and configure Firestore Security Rules to block all direct player writes to leaderboard entries."}
{"say": "Check server-issued run IDs, elapsed time, and plausible scoring limits; these catch obvious fakes, not determined cheating."}
{"say": "For stronger protection, record player inputs and replay each run server-side using deterministic game logic and a server-chosen seed."}
{"say": "The server calculates the score itself; reject reused run IDs so one run can\u2019t produce multiple submissions."}
{"say": "For your weekend project, start with basic checks, accepting some cheating risk; add replay verification if competition gets serious."}

question: That's working. Now my friends want to fly together in real time. What changes?
lines: {"say": "Keep Firebase for accounts; add an authoritative game server to synchronize ships and combat."}
{"say": "Your friends\u2019 browsers need a persistent game server, connected over WebSockets, rather than Cloud Functions handling every movement."}
{"say": "Browsers send controls, not positions; the server runs movement, enemies, collisions, and scoring for everyone."}
{"say": "Keep Firebase for accounts and leaderboards; the game server verifies login tokens, while Firestore stays outside the movement loop."}
{"say": "The server broadcasts snapshots; browsers predict their own ship\u2019s movement and smoothly interpolate other ships between updates."}
{"say": "You\u2019ll need to separate shared game rules from Phaser\u2019s rendering and host a server that supports long-lived connections."}
{"say": "Start with one two-player room, then test simulated lag and disconnects before adding matchmaking or scaling up."}

question: Let's do a server, I don't want cheaters. Can you show me the whole thing now?
lines: {"say": "Server it is: browsers send controls; the server simulates gameplay and writes Firebase scores."}
{"say": "Players sign in through Firebase Authentication, then send their login token to your game server."}
{"say": "The server verifies that token before admitting players to a room and accepting their controls over WebSockets."}
{"say": "Movement, enemies, collisions, and scoring run on the server; browsers cannot declare hits or award themselves points."}
{"say": "The server sends snapshots back; Phaser predicts your ship\u2019s movement and smoothly interpolates everyone else\u2019s."}
{"say": "When a run ends, the server writes scores directly to Firestore, replacing the old score-validation function."}
{"say": "Players can read the leaderboard, but cannot write scores; server authority blocks forged outcomes, not every cheat."}
